stem:
Adil practices mixed integer work: number-line moves, token models, and rewriting subtraction as adding the inverse. He asks whether these are separate rule books or one system.

Which two claims correctly settle that question?

options.text: Call the answer the label number line alone.
Subtracting an integer is the same as adding its inverse, on the number line and with tokens alike.
Comparison, addition, subtraction, and inverses share one coherent signed-number operation system across those representations.
Say that a finished unsigned total is what creates the signed moves he already has.

teacher.key_rationale: Integer practice uses one signed operation system: subtraction as adding the inverse holds across number line and tokens. Naming number line alone substitutes a label; reversing unsigned totals as the cause of signed moves flips the relation.
